title: Lab-automation and instrument flagships
description: Curated decisions for the lab frameworks, transports and driver packs the per-repo work depends on. Most confirm what the rules decide; the rest correct a rule (each justification says which).

overrides.justification: TypeScript/Vite React web UI for a Newton's Rings virtual lab; no Python, device-control code or simulator source ships in this commit, so it is not a device and cannot become an OpenMHS driver.
Model review of the PUB batch: a direct Driver, not a SerialDriver table: commands join a prefix and a bit-field byte ('TB' + base + '=' + chr(settings), 'CH' + channel + '=' + ...).
PyVISA SCPI driver for the Keithley 2200 series, so family-config/scpi fits.
PyVISA SCPI driver class for the Keithley 2230G, so family-config/scpi fits.
Skip: this is a Flask REST demo around a localhost TCP stub that only echoes ACK for START/STOP, so it is a fake device backend, not a real instrument API.
Chemical-kinetics ODE models with matplotlib output, not a device: no serial, VISA, USB, socket or SDK I/O and no importable device class.
Model review of the PUB batch: a direct Driver over RigolDS1054Z, not a ScpiDriver table: every channel command is assembled from parts (:CHANnel{channel}:SCALe, rigol.py:163-176).
AC Dev Lab is the lab's host/orchestration codebase, not one device driver: its device classes are MQTT clients or demo scripts over vendor SDKs, and the card's Picamera2 entry is a mock.
Matterix is a Gymnasium environment layer over Isaac Lab, not a hardware client, so family-config/gymnasium/sim-env.
pymmcore_plus_ros is a ROS 2 host application that runs a pymmcore-plus/Micro-Manager MDA and publishes images, not a device driver.
Argonne MADSci REST node standard and workcell manager; the HTTP helper talks to MADSci nodes.
serial-mcp-server is a Rust MCP server/CLI for generic serial list/open/read/write, not a device API, so skip/tooling.
Skip: SCPI/TCP control is C++20 (ScpiClient); Python only replays recordings and smoke-tests the C++ runner against its emulator.
Controls a Hamilton Vantage through PyLabRobot from a Raspberry Pi 5; a PyLabRobot-helper member (the rule labels it a driver pack).
Skip: a simulated OPC-UA chemical-plant server with a Flask HMI, not a device API.

Model review of the helper integration, 2026-11-05: the Mythen II runs over its own TCP client sls.client:Detector (sls/client.py:142) with a stop port and an upstream simulator; the Tango class is an optional Lima plugin.
Model review of wave C: a direct Driver, not a ScpiDriver table: the profile writes VSET1:<value> and ISET1:<value> with no separator, which the command-table tokenizer cannot match.
Driver pack for cameras, stages, AWGs and oscilloscopes over several transports; one card for the pack, recon picks the device class.

PyQt5 camera-control application with filter, trigger and server plugins; the camera drivers it runs are pylablib's, so the application is a host, not a driver (rule 10 saw its plugin classes and SimulatedCamera).

Model review of wave B: a direct Driver over the pack's AWG33220A class, not a ScpiDriver table (its setters transform values, amplitude sent doubled in Vpp); the scpi family keeps the card's entry symbols.
Skip: a C# WinForms Modbus TCP slave simulator with no Python wrapper, not a drivable device; a driver author can use it only as a fake PLC server to test client code.
Model review of the PUB batch: a direct Driver over SerialClient, not a SerialDriver table: a write verifies the controller with IGB or DGS and rejects an INVALID reply.
Skip: Utopia is a C#/.NET 9 MCP server of simulated household devices, not a Python driver.

Model review of wave B: a direct Driver, not the card's SerialDriver table (a direct Driver over Client instead of SerialDriver, and cap.sensing.read.v1 instead of the suggested cap.device.configure.v1)
TAVI is a McStas-backed virtual TAS GUI, not a hardware driver or Gym/MuJoCo environment, so skip/sim-env.
Model review of wave B: a direct Driver, not a SerialDriver table: the upstream assembles its S, AC, WT, PC, J and M lines from the configured axis tuple at run time.
Model review of wave B: a direct Driver, not a SerialDriver table: the upstream builds framed binary commands per channel at run time (0A 04 <channel> ... for a position query).
Model review of wave B: a direct Driver, not a SerialDriver table: each line is '/' plus the device address read at connect and an axis token ('1 move abs'), assembled at run time.
Skip: this is a physics-backed virtual SerDes instrument bench whose SCPI/TCP server controls an in-process simulated bench, so it is a fake backend for drivers, not a real DCA/BERT device.
Model review of wave C: a direct Driver, not a ScpiDriver table: LPX200.py builds each line from parts ('OPMODE=' + value, 'MODE=' + a mode name, 'REPRATE=' + a number).
Model review of recon wave A: a one-function script that saves the E4407B screen as a GIF over GPIB; it sets and measures nothing, so there is no device interface to model.
Crucible is a Rust runtime that simulates SCPI test benches, not a device driver, so bridge-runtime framework fits.
Skip: this SCPI-over-TCP/VXI-11 simulator is instrument-side, not a client driver.
Simulation-only FastAPI/Three.js web app, not a device: its PyLabRobot seam is an unimplemented scaffold, so a driver author can reuse only the bench geometry and hand-off schema.
Ocean Optics spectrometer API with a pure-Python pyseabreeze backend over pyUSB; a direct Driver over seabreeze.spectrometers.Spectrometer.

Skip: a C++ EPICS areaDetector driver for a simulated detector, not a Python device API.

rigol-scope-mcp is a Go MCP server that controls Rigol scopes over raw TCP SCPI, so it is skip/tooling rather than a Python device driver.
This is old C firmware for Droplet robots, not a Python device driver, so it is skipped.
Experiment-automation framework with a GUI and a CLI; its instrument drivers live in autolab-project/autolab-drivers, so the package is a host (rule 9 saw its pyvisa connection helpers).

This C# sample is an OPC-UA server that simulates a PLC, not a Python device driver.
BioReactorAgent is a hackathon host application, not a per-device driver: a CHO simulator and Flask/SCADA layer orchestrated around a DCS OPC-UA client.
Python 2 SCPI function module (no class) for a Keithley 2400 at GPIB address 24 via Prologix GPIB-USB, so family-config/scpi fits; port to Python 3 and supply the missing prologixGPIBUSB transport.

Guacamol is a benchmark library for de novo molecular design, not a device or simulator, so no driver applies.

Model review of wave B: a direct Driver, not a SerialDriver table: cetoniSerial builds framed binary commands (opcode, node id, CANopen index, CRC-16, DLE stuffing).

Skip: a C# .NET 5 Keysight 34465A/3458A SCPI-over-TCP emulator with no Python package, so it is a fake backend, not a drivable device.

ophyd hardware abstraction with SynAxis/SynGauss simulated devices; the post-pilot ophyd helper wraps its signals and devices.

Skip: LabUtopia is an Isaac Sim benchmark and simulation environment, not a device or a Gymnasium/MuJoCo environment.
Skip: LabUtopia is an Isaac Sim simulation benchmark for scientific embodied agents, not a device SDK or a Gymnasium/MuJoCo environment.
This JavaFX/Maven OPC UA plant simulator is not a Python device library, so the proposal is skip/not-device.
Pure-Python EPICS Channel Access client and server; the tag bridge's EPICS transport, not a device.

Skip: a CLI app driving a simulated telescope in CoppeliaSim, not a device driver; no device API exists, but its .ttt scene can serve as a fake backend; README.md:52's MIT claim lacks a LICENSE file.
camacq is a microscopy control host that orchestrates a Leica microscope through the separate leicacam client library, not a device driver.
Model review of wave B: a direct Driver over ArduinoPCR, not a SerialDriver table: a framed <...> protocol with unsolicited multi-line replies and an experiment loop.
ThermoFisherVerios is a single-device driver for the Thermo Fisher Verios SEM over the proprietary autoscript SDK; install that SDK separately and use FakeRandomMicroscope for fake runs.
Skip: this is a .NET 10 SiLA2 client test app with no Python and no device implementation, so a driver author should treat it as a SiLA2 client example, not hardware to drive.
These 2017 HF2LI measurement scripts call the vendor zhinst.utils/ziDAQServer API and define no device class, so this is prior art; a driver author would wrap that vendor SDK in one class.
Model review of wave B: a direct Driver, not a ScpiDriver table: the upstream methods assemble several VBS or SCPI lines from their arguments over a held pyvisa instrument.

orca-client is a WebSocket host that loads cheshire-drivers drivers from config and runs Orca runtime commands, not a device driver.
Skip/tooling: it writes Tecan .gwl worklists and Auto-iTC200 .xlsx files with no serial, VISA, USB or vendor SDK access; no license is declared.

Skip: motor-sim-docker only builds the upstream EPICS motor IOC with motorMotorSim, not a Python driver.

Python controller for Tricontinent C3000 syringe-pump networks (DT protocol over serial) with valve actions; a direct Driver over its pump controller classes.
Thirteen chemistry instrument classes (pumps, stirrers, thermostats) over serial and Ethernet with simulated replies; one card for the pack.
PharmaPy is a library for simulating pharmaceutical unit operations and flowsheets, not a device.
MCP server for an Andonstar USB microscope camera, not a driver library: it is a host that captures with plain OpenCV.

Skip: this is a kinematic simulation backend plus vision/skill layers for PyLabRobot's ExperimentalSCARA, not a hardware driver.

Not a device: a Tkinter/Matplotlib virtual lab plotting instrument physics equations, with no serial, VISA, USB, socket or vendor SDK.
